section: Later reorganisation of states - 1960s to 2000; creation of Telangana 2014
subsections: Jai Andhra Movement and the Six-Point Formula

accepted.s: The Telangana agitation of 1969 was led by which organisation, whose convener was A. Madan Mohan?
accepted.x: The 1969 Jai Telangana agitation was led by the Telangana Praja Samithi, with A. Madan Mohan as its convener.
accepted.tq: Identify the organisation through its associated office-bearer.
accepted.sec: Jai Andhra Movement and the Six-Point Formula

accepted.s: On which date was Indira Gandhi’s Eight-Point Formula announced in the context of the Telangana issue?
accepted.x: Prime Minister Indira Gandhi announced the Eight-Point Formula on 11 April 1969.
accepted.tq: Distinguish closely related formulas by their dates.
accepted.sec: Jai Andhra Movement and the Six-Point Formula

accepted.s: Who was the Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh when the Jai Andhra Movement began in 1972?
accepted.x: P.V. Narasimha Rao was the Chief Minister when the Jai Andhra Movement arose in 1972.
accepted.tq: Use the wrong-person trap involving political office and period.
accepted.sec: Jai Andhra Movement and the Six-Point Formula

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Jai Andhra Movement:
1. It emerged in Coastal Andhra and Rayalaseema as a counter-agitation.
2. It followed the Supreme Court judgment of October 1972 upholding the Mulki Rules.
3. Protesters hoisted a separate Andhra State flag on 10 December 1972.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The movement was a counter-agitation in Coastal Andhra and Rayalaseema, followed the October 1972 judgment, and saw the hoisting of a separate Andhra State flag on 10 December 1972.
accepted.tq: Check each statement against the movement’s region, immediate context and dated event.
accepted.sec: Jai Andhra Movement and the Six-Point Formula

accepted.s: The Mulki Rules, which became the immediate focus of the Jai Andhra agitation, had originally reserved jobs for locals under the Nizam in:
accepted.x: The Nizam’s Mulki Rules reserving jobs for locals date from 1919.
accepted.tq: Link an institutional rule with its earliest date.
accepted.sec: Jai Andhra Movement and the Six-Point Formula

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: 1972 — Supreme Court upheld the Mulki Rules and Jai Andhra agitation followed
accepted.x: The Srikrishna Committee submitted its report in 2010, not in 2001. The year 2001 is associated with the founding of the TRS by K. Chandrasekhar Rao.
accepted.tq: Find the wrong year-person or year-event pairing.
accepted.sec: Jai Andhra Movement and the Six-Point Formula

accepted.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Formation of Telangana
B. Founding of the TRS
C. Jai Telangana agitation
D. Srikrishna Committee report
accepted.x: The correct sequence is 1969 Jai Telangana agitation, 2001 founding of the TRS, 2010 Srikrishna Committee report, and 2014 formation of Telangana.
accepted.tq: Place the first and last events, then arrange the middle dates.
accepted.sec: Jai Andhra Movement and the Six-Point Formula

accepted.s: Under the Five-Point Formula of 27 November 1972, the Mulki Rules were to continue in the twin cities up to 1977 and in Telangana up to:
accepted.x: The Five-Point Formula provided for continuation of the Mulki Rules in Telangana until 1980, after which they would lapse.
accepted.tq: Separate the two regional expiry dates instead of treating them as identical.
accepted.sec: Jai Andhra Movement and the Six-Point Formula

accepted.s: Which of the following was provided under Clause 2 of the Five-Point Formula of 1972?
o: One in three Secretariat jobs were to be given to Telangana locals.
A separate Andhra State was to be created.
All Mulki Rules were to lapse immediately.
The twin-cities police were to be recruited only from Telangana.
accepted.x: Clause 2 provided that one in three Secretariat jobs should go to Telangana locals.
accepted.tq: Match a clause number with its precise administrative provision.
accepted.sec: Jai Andhra Movement and the Six-Point Formula

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Clause of the Five-Point Formula)
a. Clause 1
b. Clause 3
c. Clause 4
d. Clause 5

List-II (Provision)
i. Better educational facilities for Andhra students in the twin cities
ii. First two gazetted posts in various services localised
iii. Twin-cities police recruited from both regions
iv. Mulki Rules continued for specified periods and applied to certain posts

Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
accepted.x: Clause 1 concerned continuation and application of the Mulki Rules; Clause 3 localised the first two gazetted posts; Clause 4 concerned educational facilities; and Clause 5 concerned police recruitment.
accepted.tq: Start with the distinctive clause concerning police recruitment and eliminate codes.
accepted.sec: Jai Andhra Movement and the Six-Point Formula

accepted.s: P.V. Narasimha Rao resigned as Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh on:
accepted.x: P.V. Narasimha Rao, who had become Chief Minister on 30 September 1971, resigned on 18 January 1973.
accepted.tq: Distinguish appointment, resignation and succession dates.
accepted.sec: Jai Andhra Movement and the Six-Point Formula

accepted.s: Who became the Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh on 10 December 1973 after the end of President’s Rule?
accepted.x: Jalagam Vengala Rao became Chief Minister on 10 December 1973 after President’s Rule ended.
accepted.tq: Apply the successor trap to closely connected political figures.
accepted.sec: Jai Andhra Movement and the Six-Point Formula

accepted.s:
Which of the following pairs correctly represents the institutional changes associated with the Six-Point Formula?
1. Mulki Rules — abolition
2. Telangana Regional Committee — abolition
3. Direct recruitment — local preference in specified posts
4. Promotion disputes — special tribunal
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
accepted.x: The Six-Point Formula abolished the Mulki Rules and Telangana Regional Committee, introduced local preference in specified direct recruitment, and provided a special tribunal for promotion disputes.
accepted.tq: Combine institutional abolition with the replacement safeguards.
accepted.sec: Jai Andhra Movement and the Six-Point Formula

accepted.s: Under the Six-Point Formula, which arrangement was intended to address grievances of government employees?
o: A common police force for both successor states
A committee to select the capital at Amaravati
A committee to settle their grievances
A separate state for Coastal Andhra
accepted.x: The third point of the Six-Point Formula provided for a committee to settle government employees’ grievances.
accepted.tq: Identify the administrative remedy from the stated problem.
accepted.sec: Jai Andhra Movement and the Six-Point Formula

accepted.s: The Six-Point Formula provided for backward-area development through:
o: An Administrative Tribunal with zonal committees
A State Planning Commission with local sub-committees
A Central University with local sub-committees
The Telangana Regional Committee with district committees
accepted.x: Backward-area development was to be addressed through a State Planning Commission with local sub-committees.
accepted.tq: Distinguish planning institutions from tribunals and regional bodies.
accepted.sec: Jai Andhra Movement and the Six-Point Formula

accepted.s: Article 371E, associated with the Six-Point Formula, provides for:
o: Local cadres and six administrative zones
A State Planning Commission for backward areas
accepted.x: Article 371E provides for the establishment of a Central University at Hyderabad. Local cadres and zones are associated with Article 371D.
accepted.tq: Separate the closely related constitutional articles 371D and 371E.
accepted.sec: Jai Andhra Movement and the Six-Point Formula

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about Article 371D:
1. It is associated with local cadres and zonal arrangements.
2. It is connected with the Andhra Pradesh Administrative Tribunal.
3. It established the Central University at Hyderabad.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The Central University at Hyderabad is associated with Article 371E, not Article 371D.
accepted.tq: Use the article-number distinction to reject a swapped provision.
accepted.sec: Jai Andhra Movement and the Six-Point Formula

accepted.s: Which committee submitted a report on the separate-Telangana demand on 30 December 2010 and presented six options?
accepted.x: The Committee on Telangana headed by Justice B.N. Srikrishna submitted its report on 30 December 2010 and presented six options.
accepted.tq: Match the committee chairman with its subject and report date.
accepted.sec: Committees → chairman and mandate

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Committee or study)
a. Committee on Telangana
b. Expert Committee on AP capital
c. GN Rao Committee
d. BCG study

List-II (Association)
i. K.C. Sivaramakrishnan
 ii. Separate-Telangana demand
 iii. Basis of the three-capitals plan
 iv. Options for a new capital

Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
accepted.x: The Committee on Telangana studied the separate-state demand; the Expert Committee on AP capital was associated with K.C. Sivaramakrishnan and considered capital options; the GN Rao Committee and BCG study formed the basis of the three-capitals plan.
accepted.tq: Use the mandate first, then identify the capital-related pair.
accepted.sec: Committees → chairman and mandate

accepted.s: The Expert Committee on AP capital constituted under Section 6 was chaired by:
accepted.x: The Section 6 Expert Committee on a new capital was chaired by K.C. Sivaramakrishnan.
accepted.tq: Avoid swapping the chairmen of the Telangana and capital committees.
accepted.sec: Committees → chairman and mandate

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Expert Committee on AP capital is correct?
o: It submitted its report in December 2010 and proposed six options for Telangana.
It submitted its report in August 2014 and opposed the idea of a super capital.
It was formed in 2020 and recommended the three-capitals plan.
It selected Amaravati in 2015 after land pooling of 33,000 acres.
accepted.x: The K.C. Sivaramakrishnan Committee submitted its report in August 2014 and opposed the concept of a super capital.
accepted.tq: Distinguish committee mandate, report year and later policy outcomes.
accepted.sec: Committees → chairman and mandate

accepted.s: Amaravati was selected as the capital of Andhra Pradesh in 2015 after land pooling involving approximately:
accepted.x: Amaravati was chosen in 2015 after land pooling involving approximately 33,000 acres.
accepted.tq: Use the middle-value numerical trap for approximate figures.
accepted.sec: Committees → chairman and mandate

accepted.s: The three-capitals plan of Andhra Pradesh, associated with 2020, failed in court in:
accepted.x: The three-capitals plan introduced in 2020 failed in court in 2022.
accepted.tq: Separate the year of proposal from the year of judicial outcome.
accepted.sec: Committees → chairman and mandate

accepted.s:
The Thirteenth Schedule of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 included provisions relating to which of the following?
1. IIT, NIT, IIM and AIIMS
2. Central and tribal universities
3. A new railway zone, steel plant, port and metros
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Thirteenth Schedule included institutions such as IIT, NIT, IIM and AIIMS, central and tribal universities, and infrastructure proposals including a railway zone, steel plant, port and metros.
accepted.tq: Treat every item in a statutory schedule as a separate checklist entry.
accepted.sec: Committees → chairman and mandate
